# 'color.ui' and 'spice.color' control colored output.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-05-26T10:00:00Z'

cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'initial commit'
gs repo init

# By default, colored output follows terminal detection.
# Output is not a terminal in tests, so it is not colored.
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

# color.ui=always forces colored output.
git config color.ui always
gs log short
stderr '\x1b\['

# color.ui=false disables colored output,
# even when the environment requests it.
git config color.ui false
env CLICOLOR_FORCE=1
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

# spice.color overrides color.ui.
git config spice.color always
gs log short
stderr '\x1b\['

git config color.ui always
git config spice.color never
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

# Automatic mode respects disabling environment variables.
# Force terminal detection because script output is captured.
git config color.ui auto
git config spice.color auto
env CLICOLOR_FORCE=0
env TTY_FORCE=1
env TERM=xterm-256color
gs log short
stderr '\x1b\['

env NO_COLOR=please
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

env NO_COLOR=0
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

env NO_COLOR=
env CLICOLOR=0
gs log short
! stderr '\x1b'

# Explicit configuration takes precedence over environment defaults.
git config spice.color always
gs log short
stderr '\x1b\['

-- repo/README.md --
# Test repository
